image_description: A side-profile view of a vintage light-blue minibus parked on an asphalt surface. The vehicle features a boxy design with a row of rectangular side windows, a sliding door track visible above the windows, and standard steel wheels with hubcaps. There is yellow text on the side panel that appears to be gibberish or stylized non-Latin script. A brick wall and green foliage are visible in the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle exhibits the classic short-wheelbase, high-roof proportions of a minibus (resembling a VW Type 2). The height relative to the wheel diameter suggests adequate interior headroom.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large front windshield is partially visible, and a clear row of four distinct side windows runs along the passenger compartment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has a high roofline. A vertical seam indicating a sliding door is visible between the front driver window and the first passenger window.
The vertical gap and the horizontal rail/track visible above the window line confirm the presence of a sliding door mechanism.
The short overhang ahead of the front wheel indicates a compact engine bay, typical of rear-engine or compact front-engine minibuses.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped at the rear bumper; the back panel, taillights, and license plate are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus is painted light blue with yellow lettering on the side, fitting the description of a company livery.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two wheels are clearly visible, featuring standard steel rims with hubcaps, consistent with vintage van/minibus specifications.
The number of side windows (4) implies seating capacity consistent with the 4-10 passenger range.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The yellow text on the side of the bus is illegible and structurally nonsensical, resembling AI-generated 'fake text' rather than a real language or logo.
The reflections in the side windows are vague and muddy, lacking the sharp specular highlights expected from glass. The interior details behind the glass are indistinct and painterly.
The front headlight and bumper geometry is slightly soft and lacks precise mechanical definition, blending into the bodywork more than a real stamped-metal vehicle would.

selected_experts.reason: To verify the specific make/model consistency and ensure the vehicle is correctly classified as a minibus despite the vintage style.
To analyze the gibberish yellow text and confirm it is an artifact rather than a stylized font or foreign language.
To check for edge bleeding between the bus and the background, and to ensure the sliding door track and window frames are topologically connected correctly.
To assess the overall realism, lighting consistency, and texture quality of the metal and glass surfaces.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of the yellow side text
Geometric precision of the wheel hubs and tire contact patches
Clarity and reflectivity of the side windows
Sharpness of the door seams and body lines
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. While the vehicle structure is largely sound, the text is a definitive AI indicator. Also, evaluate if the 'vintage' aesthetic is being used to mask low-frequency texture errors in the metal bodywork. Check if the wheel geometry is perfectly circular or slightly warped.
